settings.scope: architecture measurement across five decision gates

deviations.summary: Trials ran on development runtime 25.0.4 rather than the pinned Mojang 25.0.1; setting RAVEL_SPIKE_JAVA to the pinned runtime removes the difference. Every gate carries it, so the figures are comparable to each other and none is a measurement of the runtime players use.

Boundary-traffic figures are computed from each trial's known signature rather than counted by an instrument, yet are recorded as measured with a collector identity. The arithmetic is correct and no conclusion rests on it.

Retained RSS and bootstrap peak RSS come from one /proc read taken at the ready marker before any measured invocation, so they are byte-identical in every ADG-1, ADG-2 and ADG-4 result and measure no workload-retained memory.
ADG-4 describes one flow under three owners, but the three models differ by two Java field writes and one addition, so argument size is confounded with a small difference in work done.

Seven of twenty results record a trial.revision.id that cannot be reconstructed as described: six ADG-1 results name a predecessor of their own change, and the ADG-5 result names a change above the one holding it. The checked half, trial.revision.changeId, is correct on all twenty and is recomputed by ravel:verify-spikes. Nothing reads the commit field.

ADG-5 records a stock launch as three substring tests over a redacted log. Nothing verifies the launched version, the launcher identity, that the arguments sat on the game command line, or that the client reached a world or exited cleanly. The record used to overstate that: prismIntegration.detail asserted the pinned game launched with both arguments on its command line and no other mod loader named, which is a conclusion the three tests do not reach, and only evidence/m1/README.md said so honestly. The record now states the three tests and what they leave unchecked, and experiments/adg-5-prism/src/main.rs was changed in the same pass so a re-run of the gate writes the same sentence rather than restoring the old one.
schemas/package.schema.json still requires per-target mod artifacts, which SPEC 3.4 no longer promises. It is disclosed there by name as an inherited assumption and is owned by M3.

The recorded digest of docs/architecture/m1-measurement-gate.md was taken from an intermediate state of this change and matched the file at no revision reachable from the history. It is corrected to the digest the pinned revision holds; the gate now recomputes every input digest there, so the drift cannot recur silently.

This manifest does not exist at the revision it pins. revision.id 909240424db4 is an abandoned predecessor state of change potzkxqsxykqpvzylkqpspmvvsxzoqrt, and evidence/m1/manifest.json is absent from it: the manifest was written into change rxovtruttmykusmvquqkuqqtqwousopz after that commit existed, and jj rewrote rxovtruttmyk afterwards, so no commit that holds this file is reachable from the one its provenance field names. That is the same defect this evidence calls worse about the ADG-5 spike result, disclosed there and for the six ADG-1 results and not, until now, for the manifest itself. It matters because the doc comment on verify_recorded_inputs in tools/ravel-xtask/src/lib.rs reads revision.id as the commit the milestone was measured against, and a reader may take that to mean the manifest describes that tree. There is no live drift: all five recorded input digests match at that revision and the gate recomputes them there on every run, which is the one thing the field binds. It is disclosed rather than repaired because both repairs replace a true statement with a false one. The recorded commands did run on 909240424db4, so re-pinning id to a commit that holds this file would falsify the commands and tests blocks; and re-running the gate to make those numbers a later tree's is a re-measurement of M1 that nobody has asked for and that would land one change below whatever commit recorded it, which is the circularity evidence/m3/manifest.json carries in its own revision block.

M1-W4's ROADMAP Verification clause asks that a generated 26.1.2 binding be reproducible from pinned inputs and fail on drift. The drift half is recorded: both measured ADG-3 results record bindingGeneration.driftDetected true. The reproducibility half is not recorded anywhere in M1, and this deviation states that plainly rather than rewording the clause. bindingGeneration.outputSha256 is written once per candidate, and the two extractors' outputs differ — 0ecc36a9 over 3417 bytes for classfile against 8b093021 over 3413 bytes for javap — so the cross-extractor digest cannot stand in for a repeated run, and README's line that two independent extractors resolved all six targets identically comes from a prose string in both records with no per-target list recorded, which makes it attested rather than recomputable. M2 carries an explicit repeatedRunIsIdentical field for exactly this; M1's schema has no field for it, since schemas/spike-result.schema.json fixes bindingGeneration at driftDetected, durationMs, outputBytes, and outputSha256 with additional properties refused. What does bind it is the experiment source rather than the evidence: experiments/adg-3-bindings/src/bin/generate.rs generates the binding twice from the same resolved inventory and refuses to report at all if the two digests differ, so a recorded ADG-3 result entails one identical repeat. That is an entailment from the instrument's source at the revision it ran, not a recorded observation, and no gate recomputes it. Recording one now is not available: the generator's input model refuses unknown fields and minecraft/versions/26.1.2/adapter.toml has since grown dataFixerJar, stubSeeds, mappingsLock, and stubsLock, so bindings::adapter refuses to parse it and the M1 generator cannot run against today's pinned inputs. Editing the experiment to make it run would measure a different instrument than the one M1 recorded. The clause is therefore unmet by the recorded evidence, and it is the one ROADMAP Verification clause in M1 that is.

The cold audit returned FAIL with ten findings. All ten were resolved and none has been re-audited, so the last cold verdict recorded against this evidence is FAIL. review.result records fail accordingly. It previously recorded pass, which contradicted this deviation in the same file and made a recorded pass mean one thing here and another in evidence/m3/manifest.json, where the identical situation is recorded as fail. M3's convention is the one kept, so ravel:verify-milestone:m1 now reports the review as outstanding until a cold auditor re-verifies this evidence.

risks.summary: The selected native binding has never run in the real game. The observed ADG-5 launch used ADG-1's Java-callback variant, so the exported-symbol path is unexercised outside the spike harness. M2-W5 owns closing this.
The measured hot path carries no panic guard, and the veto-by-throwing hook shape named first in hooks.toml was never measured. 10.02 ns is the unguarded cost.

ADG-2 retains the dynamic library as a live M3 candidate although it needs two maintained unsafe calls, which the M1 gate failure actions otherwise reject. Selecting it requires a SPEC 3.3 amendment and a safety-boundary row.
The linked candidate's mod-to-mod path is unguarded and crosses extern C, so a panic there aborts exactly as the dynamic library does. Guarding it costs something this gate did not measure.

review.reviewer: independent Claude reviewer (M1 architecture, four passes) with a separate cold audit
